default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1278.title: Dollar-lead catch-up
E-1278.hypothesis: A strong move of the dollar contract that the index has not yet matched is an inverse-correlation lag: arbitrageurs and macro desks transmit it to WIN within minutes; trade WIN in the implied direction.

E-1279.title: Day-open reclaim
E-1279.hypothesis: After the price spent a while on one side of the session open, a close back across it shows the opening-auction participants flipping from trapped to in control; follow the cross.

E-1280.title: Absorption bar break
E-1280.hypothesis: A bar with heavy volume but a small range means one side absorbed the other's orders; the next close beyond that bar's extreme shows which side was left holding.

E-1281.title: ATR-stretch snap-back
E-1281.hypothesis: When the price is stretched several average bar-ranges from its EMA, the first bar that closes back toward it shows the chasers are exhausted; fade toward the mean.

E-1282.title: Final-hour VWAP reversion
E-1282.hypothesis: In the last hour, institutional benchmark orders (VWAP) and position squaring pull the price toward the day's VWAP when it has strayed further than usual for that minute.

E-1283.title: Lunch squeeze break
E-1283.hypothesis: A midday range much narrower than usual for the same time shows liquidity withdrawn; the first close beyond it is the side that commits when the afternoon flow arrives.

E-1284.title: Thin-volume shock fade
E-1284.hypothesis: A bar return several standard deviations large but on below-normal volume is a small order moving a thin book, not information; the move tends to retrace.

E-1285.title: Session-range midpoint cross
E-1285.hypothesis: The midpoint of the day's range is the balance level; after the price lived on one side of it, a close through it shows the other side taking over the day's auction.

E-1286.title: Expanding-bar blow-off fade
E-1286.hypothesis: Three consecutive closes in one direction with growing bar ranges that print a fresh extreme look like a climactic stop-run; fade it.

E-1287.title: Choppy-regime range fade
E-1287.hypothesis: When Kaufman's efficiency ratio is low the market is mean-reverting noise; a close beyond the recent range in such a regime is a false break and should be faded.
